title: Do not list GitHub's default pull_request activity types in workflow triggers
answers: workflow runs twice or the trigger types are redundant after my edit
why does conftest deny types: opened synchronize reopened on pull_request
how do I declare pull_request types in a GitHub workflow in this repo
can I write types for pull_request_target that match the defaults
body:
Invariant: a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` trigger must not declare `types` equal to GitHub's defaults {opened, synchronize, reopened}; omit `types` so GitHub applies them implicitly.
Enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_default_pull_request_types, which compares the set of listed types to `default_pull_request_types` for each of the two events and emits a message naming the trigger.
The check is exact set equality: omitted `types`, a subset (e.g. only `opened`), or a superset with extra types such as `labeled` are all allowed and not flagged.
What breaks if skipped: conftest fails the workflow check. Behavior is unchanged either way, since the listed types equal the defaults.
Constraints: keep `paths`, `paths-ignore` and branch filters when removing `types`; the PR removed only the `types` block from 16 workflows. Adding a non-default type is the way to keep an explicit `types` list.
applies: `on:` pull_request and pull_request_target triggers in .github/workflows/*.yml; does not cover other events such as push or issue triggers.
says: Continuous integration policy check fails when pull request triggers specify default activity types.
Why is our automated workflow linting failing on default pull request event configurations?
Automated pull request checks fail validation because standard trigger events were explicitly listed.
Omit standard pull request activity types so workflow policy verification passes during builds.
Prevent policy compliance failures by removing default event triggers from automation workflows.
search: GitHub workflow triggers for pull_request and pull_request_target must omit the types filter if it exactly matches GitHub's default set of opened, synchronize, and reopened. This policy is enforced by conftest via .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_default_pull_request_types, which flags exact set equality against default_pull_request_types while permitting omitted types, subsets like opened alone, or supersets including non-default types such as labeled. When removing redundant types blocks, existing paths, paths-ignore, and branch filters must be retained. The rule applies specifically to on: pull_request and pull_request_target triggers in .github/workflows/*.yml, without covering push or issue triggers.
